title: When Does Qubit Decoherence Require a Non-Markovian Model?
problem:
When do finite, noisy observations of a qubit justify a non-Markovian dynamical model instead of a simpler Markovian explanation? Develop a falsifiable, evidence-calibrated account of quantum memory in an open two-level system. Do not assume that revivals, non-exponential decay, time-dependent rates, or apparently improved fits establish non-Markovianity.

BOUNDARIES AND DEFINITIONS. Explicitly identify the operational definition used in each claim: CP divisibility of a family of dynamical maps, information backflow as a trace-distance increase between distinguishable initial states, process-tensor memory under interventions, or a classical hidden-variable / colored-noise explanation. These definitions can disagree; do not silently treat one diagnostic as equivalent to all others. State assumptions about initial system-environment correlations, preparation, control, measurement, stationarity, and map invertibility. Keep the reduced-system dynamical model distinct from claims about the microscopic environment.

TRACTABLE MODEL. Begin with a single-qubit dephasing or amplitude-damping model in which an exactly specified time-local rate or decoherence function permits analytic derivations and reproducible synthetic trajectories. Construct a Markovian baseline (for example a physically valid semigroup or suitably defined CP-divisible dynamics), one explicitly non-CP-divisible candidate, and one alternative that can mimic apparent memory under sparse sampling, preparation drift, SPAM errors, or slowly varying classical noise. Specify complete positivity and physical parameter bounds. Do not call time inhomogeneity alone non-Markovian.

DISCRIMINATING OBSERVATIONS. Derive what measurements could actually distinguish the candidates. Examine populations, coherence, distinguishability of multiple initial states, controlled interventions where feasible, and dependence on sampling times and noise. Do not infer a process-tensor result from single-time state tomography. Evaluate model identifiability: demonstrate an observationally equivalent or nearly equivalent pair of explanations over a finite window where possible, and propose extra measurements that break the degeneracy.

QUANTITATIVE TEST. Pre-register a synthetic study or, if suitable publicly accessible data are verified, a held-out empirical comparison. Specify the likelihood/noise model, state-preparation and measurement uncertainty, time sampling, train/test split, parameter constraints, complexity penalties, and calibration of confidence. Compare a valid Markovian null with at least one non-Markovian alternative and a confounder baseline using predictive performance, false-positive rate, statistical power, and robustness across noise/sample regimes. Simulated data are not experimental evidence; label all results accordingly. Do not claim to have run code or experiments without reproducible outputs.

SCIENTIFIC TARGET. Seek a precise conditional criterion for when specified evidence justifies rejecting a specified Markovian null, or prove an identifiability limitation for a defined class of measurements. Benchmark against published criteria before claiming novelty. Produce a defensible theoretical or computational result if possible, with explicit assumptions, derivations, counterexamples, code/parameters if used, and uncertainty. If no genuinely new result survives prior-art review and adversarial testing, report a rigorous negative result or research plan instead of inventing a discovery. A review of known tests is not automatically original research.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA FOR A VALID RESEARCH OUTCOME. The investigation must (1) state a precise, answerable scientific claim or a well-defined identifiability question, with the relevant definition of non-Markovianity and physical assumptions; (2) establish what is already known through traceable primary literature, and distinguish established results from reproduced calculations, new deductions, simulations, and conjectures; (3) support every substantive conclusion with inspectable mathematical derivations, physically admissible models, verified source evidence, or reproducible computation as applicable, without inventing observations or executions; (4) test the claim against at least one genuinely competing Markovian explanation and one plausible experimental or modeling confounder, including a concrete attempted falsification or counterexample; (5) account for finite sampling, noise, state-preparation and measurement limitations, model complexity, and uncertainty when drawing inferences from data; (6) define the scope of any positive conclusion, including circumstances in which the evidence does not identify a unique mechanism; and (7) identify remaining proof obligations, contradictory evidence, and decisive follow-up tests. A novel result is acceptable only if distinct from prior work and independently substantiated within its stated scope. A rigorous negative finding, impossibility or non-identifiability result, or a clearly evidenced unresolved conclusion also counts as valid research. A plausible explanation, literature summary alone, or attractive but untested hypothesis does not satisfy the criteria.

strategies.title: Establish definitions and analytic baselines
strategies.approach: Review primary literature on CP divisibility, trace-distance backflow and operational process-tensor memory, stating their distinct assumptions and implications. Derive a concrete qubit dephasing or amplitude-damping family with explicit Kraus/map or master-equation representations. Check physicality and initial-state assumptions, and specify at least one CP-divisible baseline and one non-CP-divisible countermodel. Identify known results versus potentially new deductions; avoid conflating colored classical noise with a unique microscopic quantum environment.
strategies.summary: A traceable literature baseline, exact model equations, physicality conditions and clearly scoped definitions.

strategies.title: Test identifiability under finite noisy measurement
strategies.approach: Construct competing models that produce similar sampled populations/coherences yet differ under a precisely defined memory criterion. Specify measurement times, realistic finite-shot/SPAM assumptions and controlled initial states. Derive or compute bounds on distinguishability and construct a counterexample to naive claims that oscillation, revival or improved fit alone establishes memory. Identify additional time points, preparations, or interventions that discriminate; state when even these are insufficient.
strategies.summary: A concrete observational degeneracy or identifiable regime with explicit counterexamples and decisive measurements.

strategies.title: Adversarial model selection and reproducible validation
strategies.approach: Specify and, if computation is available, execute a preregistered simulation with reproducible seeds, valid parameter ranges, train/held-out time points, likelihoods, uncertainty, and sensitivity analysis. Compare Markovian null, non-Markovian alternative, and drift/colored-noise confounder; measure false positives, power, predictive fit and complexity penalties. Seek known statistical and physics counterarguments, test robustness to SPAM, undersampling and model misspecification, and demand verifiable evidence before a novelty claim. Mark any unexecuted experiments as proposals.
strategies.summary: An adversarial, reproducible model-comparison protocol with calibrated conclusions or a documented negative result.
